info.bio:
Death Cab For Cutie es un grupo de indie-rock original de Bellingham, Washington. Se formó en 1997 y toma su nombre de una canción escrita por Vivian Stanshall, que forma parte del disco Gorilla (1967) de The Bonzo Dog Band y de la película experimental de The Beatles: Magical Mistery Tour.

Death Cab For Cutie comenzó como un proyecto en solitario de Ben Gibbard mientras era el guitarrista de Pinwheel. Como "Death Cab for Cutie",  Gibbard editó un primer cassette llamado You Can Play These Songs With Chords.

scenes.desc: Una de las innovaciones más importantes de los noventa: versión lenta, onírica y melancólica del dream-pop, descendiente de Galaxie 500 y Yo La Tengo, con composiciones largas y contenidas. Codeine la consagran (Frigid Stars); Seam, Red House Painters de Mark Kozelek (Down Colorful Hill), Low (I Could Live In Hope, Trust: el haiku del rock) y Bedhead. La balada etérea femenina: Mazzy Star, His Name Is Alive, Moon Seven Times, Congo Norvell, Helium, Elysian Fields. La balada atmosférica: Idaho, Acetone, Low Road, American Analog Set, Calla, y el «rock textural» del Noroeste: Built To Spill (Perfect From Now On), Silkworm, Red Stars Theory, Death Cab For Cutie. En Inglaterra, Drugstore, Mojave 3, Movietone.

podcast.title: Anti-Auto-Tune Stance
podcast.body: Death Cab for Cutie maintains a strong opposition to the use of auto-tune, declaring themselves "100% dead against" it and proclaiming "death to auto-tune at every available opportunity." The band, including Ben Gibbard, ensures their recordings are "uncorrected," representing the authentic sound of the band working together in a studio without pitch modification. "They are 100% dead against the use of auto-tune."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Appeal to Tweetpop Fans
podcast.body: Death Cab for Cutie is mentioned as a band that appeals to Tweetpop fans, implying their music aligns with the genre's introspective, melodic, and emotionally sensitive qualities. This makes them a fitting choice for listeners who identify as shy, introspective, and find much contemporary music too loud or aggressive. "And the decemberists tend to appeal to most Tweet fans, same thing with Death Cab for Cutie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Guest Musician on Sonic Highways
podcast.body: Ben Gibbert, from the band Death Cab for Cutie, was a local guest musician featured on the Foo Fighters' song "Subterranean" from the "Sonic Highways" album. The track was recorded at Robert Lang Studios north of Seattle. "The local guest for this track was Ben Gibbert of Death Cab for Cutie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Long-Distance Running Hobby
podcast.body: Ben Gibbard has a particular enthusiasm for long-distance running. "Ben Gibber of Death Cab for Cutie had a thing for long distance running."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Twilight Soundtracks Contribution
podcast.body: Death Cab for Cutie contributed to the various *Twilight* soundtracks that accompanied the film series. These soundtracks featured a nice selection of tunes, mostly album cuts and outtakes, from a range of artists spanning different genres. "The Paramore, Lincoln Park, Collective Soul, Death Cab for Cutie, Tom York, the Killers, Editors, Metric, Block Keys, Dead Weather, Beck, Vampire Weekend, Florence in the Machine."

xref.title: Industry Recognition and Collaborations
xref.body: Their talent garnered attention from prominent musicians; Jack White was such a fan that The White Stripes recorded one of their songs. They also developed friendships with members of Death Cab for Cutie and embarked on tours with acclaimed artists such as Neil Young, Weezer, The Black Keys, Cake, Bryan Adams, and Sious and Colour. "Jack White was such a fan that the white stripes recorded one of their songs. They became friends with members of Death Cab for Cutie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
